newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi gets strong Galant, Legnum orders.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi gets strong Galant, Legnum orders.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Wednesday it received 19,000 domestic orders for its new Galant sedan and Legnum station wagon in the first month after they were launched on August 29 with a combined monthly sales target of 7,000.
Of the total of 9,500 orders for the Galant, some 90 percent were for Galants equipped with a new 1.8-litre gasoline direct injection (GDI) fuel-efficient engine, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
Thirty-six percent of the 9,500 orders for the Legnum wagon were for those powered by GDI engines.

Mitsubishi says its GDI engine can reduce the amount of fuel consumption by 35 percent compared with its predecessor, while reducing emissions of carbon dioxide by 35 percent and increasing engine power by 10 percent.

As a result of strong demand for GDI engined cars, Mitsubishi's Kyoto plant in western Japan will boost its production of the GDI engine to a total of 26,000 units between October and March from a previously planned 18,000, the spokesman said.
The Kyoto plant will operate for up to two extra days each month from October until December to achieve the increased production, he said.
